title: UPDATE: Claude Debunks 25 Year NSA Backdoor Theory on NIST Seeds
summary:
The Claude AI model identified the specific origin of the NIST P-256 seed in less than 30 minutes, providing mathematical evidence that resolves 25 years of speculation that the NSA hid a backdoor in the curve seeds. The model found the seed was candidate #1842 from a random number generator that started at 01:52:34 UTC on August 16, 1997. In a separate development, independent researchers improved an elliptic curve quantum circuit design by Anthropic, reducing the gate count to 11.9M at 843 qubits compared to Claude's 21M gates.

These results build on a research collaboration between Anthropic and Harvard where Claude Mythos 5 outperformed established benchmarks on seven of eight quantum circuit design tasks. The model operated in a closed loop using the OpenEvolve tool to propose architectures and refine them based on an automated evaluator. This work included the first reversible implementation of the divsteps algorithm, which reduces the resources required for quantum applications in materials science and chemistry.

selectedTweets.bestBit: LLM-proposed quantum circuits beat the best-known designs on seven of eight tasks, with fewer Toffoli gates and fewer qubits
selectedTweets.text:
Banger paper from Anthropic, Harvard, and colleagues.

They find that LLM-proposed quantum circuits beat the best-known designs on seven of eight tasks, with fewer Toffoli gates and fewer qubits.

They search over these circuit-generating programs with OpenEvolve, using Claude Mythos 5 to propose architectures and program rewrites.

LLMs propose circuit designs, an independent evaluator verifies correctness and scores the cost, and the best designs seed the next round.

The tasks cover numerical computation, chemistry, optimization, quantum simulation, and number theory.

On the eighth task, the search found a new reversible architecture for prime-field modular inversion. It makes divsteps, a classical algorithm impractical for reversible arithmetic, usable and improves the Toffoli-qubit trade-off.

The evaluator verifies every circuit before scoring, so each reported gain is a checked circuit.

https://t.co/8hHTwMfKHS
